Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

recent adjective

also latest, the latest, most recent, in recent years, in recent days, newly, newly built, new-born

classical

Caes. BG 1.14: recentium injūriārum memoriam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 8.15.2: recentissima tua est epistula Kal. data
Traupman 369

recēns, recentis

adjective, third declension, one ending

recent, not long past; fresh

“That has not long existed”, as against novus, “not there before” (Lewis & Short). Within more recent memory: recentiōre memoriā (Cic. N.D. 2.6, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • proximus, proxima, proximum — most recent, last

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.1: proximā nocte

    The nearest in time, before or after (see last: the one before this).

  • nūper — recently, lately

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. NH 15.82: nūper excōgitātum est

    A recent invention is something nūper excōgitātum (see lately).

Examples

  • recentissima tua est epistula Kal. data, in quā optās congressum pācemque nōn dēspērās

    your most recent letter is dated the Kalends; in it you hope for a meeting and do not despair of peaceCic. Att. 8.15.2

  • nātūrā locus jam ante praeceps recentī lāpsū terrae in pedum mīlle admodum altitūdinem abruptus erat

    the place, steep by nature already, had been broken away by a recent landslide to a depth of nearly a thousand feetLiv. 21.36.2

See also lately, new, last.
